name: Collect data with a digital tool
description: Student can collect data for a categorical or numerical variable using a digital tool.
exampleOfSuccess: The student uses a class poll or spreadsheet to gather responses.
commonError: Student collects data inconsistently or loses responses.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to collect a small data set using a digital tool.

name: Make a many-to-one pictograph
description: Student can make a pictograph where one symbol represents more than one item, with a key.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a pictograph where one symbol stands for 5, with a key.
commonError: Student treats each symbol as one item, ignoring the scale.
checkpointTask: Give a data set. Ask the student to make a many-to-one pictograph with a key.

name: Make a column graph with a scale
description: Student can make a column graph with a suitable scale.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a column graph with a scale of 2 and labelled axes.
commonError: Student uses a scale of 1 for large data, or an uneven scale.
checkpointTask: Give a data set with larger values. Ask the student to make a column graph.

name: Interpret a many-to-one display
description: Student can read and interpret a many-to-one display using its key or scale.
exampleOfSuccess: Using the key, the student reads that a row of 4 symbols means 20.
commonError: Student reads the symbols as ones, ignoring the key.
checkpointTask: Show a many-to-one display. Ask the student to read and interpret the values.

name: Suggest questions a display answers
description: Student can suggest questions that a given data display can answer.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown a graph, the student asks 'Which was most popular?'
commonError: Student asks a question the display cannot answer.
checkpointTask: Show a display. Ask the student what questions it could answer.

name: Compare two displays of the same data
description: Student can compare two displays of the same data and describe differences.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the column graph shows the totals more clearly than the table.
commonError: Student describes one display without comparing.
checkpointTask: Show two displays of the same data. Ask the student to compare them.

name: Describe the shape of the data
description: Student can describe the shape of a data distribution, such as where most values fall.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says most students scored in the middle, with few at the ends.
commonError: Student reads single values without describing the overall shape.
checkpointTask: Show a data display. Ask the student to describe where most of the data falls.

name: Judge which display suits the data
description: Student can judge which display is most suitable for a data set and explain why.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a column graph suits comparing categories better than a list.
commonError: Student picks a display with no reason, or one that hides the comparison.
checkpointTask: Show a data set and options. Ask the student which display suits it and why.

name: Design a survey
description: Student can design a survey to collect data for an investigation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes a clear survey question with set response options.
commonError: Student writes a vague or leading question.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to design a survey question for an investigation.

name: Collect and record data digitally
description: Student can collect survey data and record it using a digital tool.
exampleOfSuccess: The student records responses in a spreadsheet as they come in.
commonError: Student records data in a way that cannot be totalled.
checkpointTask: Have the student run a survey and record the data digitally.

name: Display the investigation data
description: Student can display the data from their investigation suitably.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a column graph of the survey results.
commonError: Student chooses a display that does not suit the data.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to display their investigation data.

name: Communicate the findings
description: Student can interpret and communicate the results of their investigation in context.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 'most chose the comedy, so that is the class movie'.
commonError: Student reports numbers without answering the investigation question.
checkpointTask: After the investigation, ask the student what the data shows about the question.
